analysis.title: Lennox International Inc. (LII): Lowering estimates on weaker Resi HVAC
key_insights: GS lowers FY26/FY27/FY28 EPS to $21.15/$23.05/$24.85 from $23.15/$24.95/$26.70 on weaker Home Comfort Solutions (HCS) price realization and higher tariff and inflation costs. Rating stays Neutral.

12-month price target cut to $357 from $390, based on 11.0x (vs 11.5x prior) Q5-Q8 EBITDA. The lower multiple reflects limited visibility and a weaker Resi growth outlook. Stock at $332.64 implies 7.3% upside.
3Q26 adj. EPS was $6.84 vs consensus $7.37. Segment EBIT was 7% below Visible Alpha consensus, driven by weaker HCS sales and margins, partly offset by Building Climate Solutions (BCS).
HCS sales were -1% organically (vs -9% in 2Q). Direct-to-contractor was -6% (vs -12% in 2Q) and two-step was +13% against easy destocking comparisons. Volume/price+mix/other was -3%/+2%/+4%.

HCS mix/price contributed only +$13mn, against a -$32mn product cost/absorption headwind and -$15mn of fuel, SG&A and distribution inflation. LII used dynamic pricing, taking targeted price cuts in select regions and customer segments to defend share.

GS views the need to give up price to hold position in core replacement as a weaker competitive standing, particularly in the entry tier (overseas entrants and value brands gaining traction) and in Resi national accounts, where LII acknowledges it must refresh its value proposition. Management says there was no incremental share loss beyond RNC.

LII's four-pronged recovery plan (pricing, productivity, portfolio, promoters) includes a full entry-tier launch in 1Q27 and resizing of residential capacity and distribution. GS sees it as directionally right but a multi-quarter effort with execution risk, and expects Resi HVAC share loss to persist well into next year.

BCS sales were +24% (+6% vs consensus, +15% organic), with volume/price+mix/other of +13%/+2%/+9%. EBIT margin was 26.2%, 30bps above consensus, driven by Emergency Replacement, national accounts and services.
BCS price-cost was negative as national account contract pricing lags. Management now expects roughly flat FY26 BCS margins.
LII cut its FY26 EPS guidance to $21.00-$21.50 from $23.00-$24.00, on total sales growth of about +6% (vs Visible Alpha +7.6%), including a +5% acquisition impact.

GS says price realization and share recapture could prove difficult to achieve simultaneously. It cites BCS momentum, strong cash conversion, self-help levers and a valuation that has already de-rated as support, but lacks visibility on when Resi price/cost turns positive.
LII shares are down 38.9% over 3 months, 32.9% over 6 months and 33.6% over 12 months, underperforming the S&P 500 by 41.2%, 37.9% and 40.8%.

sector_views.rationale: GS expects share loss, pricing pressure and entry-tier competition at LII to persist well into next year. Resi affordability remains pressured.
BCS is described as a bright spot, with +15% organic growth and 26.2% EBIT margin, though national account pricing lags and FY26 margins are expected roughly flat.

tension_points.bull_case: BCS momentum, strong cash conversion, identifiable self-help levers and a valuation that has already de-rated meaningfully support the stock. The four-pronged recovery plan (pricing, productivity, portfolio, promoters) is directionally right.
tension_points.bear_case: LII had to cut price to hold share in core replacement, entry-tier competitors are gaining traction, and price realization and share recapture may not be achievable at once. GS expects Resi share loss to persist well into next year.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A stronger Resi replacement recovery, sustained BCS share gains, or better returns from growth initiatives (the report's stated upside risks) would challenge the bear case. Resi price/cost turning positive would also matter, but the report gives no date or level.

theme_stances.key_argument: LII needed to sacrifice price to hold position in core replacement, which GS reads as a weaker competitive standing.
theme_stances.evidence: we view the need to sacrifice price simply to hold position
